summary: Maintain current step execution clocks instead of replaying retained timing history on work reads

replay.detail: A local current-attempt clock projection is rebuilt from canonical timing claims once on upgrade and on explicit replay. Ordinary in-order timing claims update its raw accumulator transactionally. Late claims, canonical metadata corrections, body repairs, deletions and attempt changes refold the affected step. Replication admission marks pending source changes; projection completion flushes the same maintenance path. Pending reads, older snapshots and historical attempts use the reference fold.

schema.detail: Adds local_step_clocks, local_step_clock_pending and local_step_clock_dirty, with an indexed pending-subject queue and source invalidation triggers. These rebuildable local tables are excluded from shared authority digests and replication.

rules.detail: Canonical timing semantics and checkpoint retention remain unchanged. Snapshot settlement never mutates the raw accumulator. Quiet local lease extensions remain separate from the lease recorded by timing claims.

compatibility.detail: Existing stores build the local projection from retained authoritative claims. Work response fields and timing results are unchanged. Metrics add bounded operation/reason counters for projection hits, fallback reasons, reference fold calls, refolds and events visited; no entity identities label them.

downtime.detail: The first open rebuilds current clocks from retained step timing claims once; subsequent opens flush only pending or invalidated clocks.

manual.detail: No operator steps or source migration required.

recovery.detail: The claim log remains authoritative. Replaying projections rebuilds clocks. Binary rollback ignores the local clock projection and restores reference reads without losing timing history.
